question: Since 2023, organised criminal networks – documented by international investigative journalism1 – have been producing and selling commissioned videos of domestic animal torture, primarily targeting cats, for up to USD 1 300 per video on Telegram23. Minors have been documented within these distribution networks. Does the Council intend to: 1.

confirm that animal torture videos disseminated on a platform registered under the Digital Services Act4 (DSA) – where such content is illegal under applicable animal protection laws in one or more Member States – constitute illegal content within the meaning of Article 3(h) of the DSA, and indicate what measures it envisages to ensure effective and durable removal by Telegram within the timeframes set by the DSA;

support or initiate a verification procedure of the monthly active user figures declared by Telegram in the EU5 and consider revisiting the 45-million-user designation threshold for very large online platforms to ensure that platforms posing a systemic risk – particularly for illegal content involving vulnerable individuals or minors – are subject to enhanced obligations;

coordinate action with national Digital Services Coordinators and Europol to initiate formal DSA compliance proceedings against Telegram, given the transnational, organised and commercial nature of these networks and the documented involvement of minors?

CNN, May 2025; Franceinfo, September 2025; Le Temps. Telegram is registered under Regulation (EU) 2022/2065 (DSA) with a legal representative in the Union (EDSR SA, Brussels). The dissemination of animal cruelty footage constitutes illegal content under the laws of several Member States.

However, Telegram has not been designated a very large online platform under Article 33 of the DSA, as it declares fewer than 45 million monthly active users in the Union, significantly reducing its moderation obligations. Despite repeated civil society reports, dedicated groups systematically reappear following each removal.

3 Over 12 000 such videos have been catalogued in three years by the Feline Guardians and Les Gardiens des Félins collectives. Between June 2024 and February 2025, this content increased by 500 % across monitored Telegram groups. The Royal Society for the Prevention of Cruelty to Animals (RSPCA) reported a 27 % rise in related reports in the United Kingdom in 2025.
